 Imd Steps Up Rain Alert For Telangana Under Cyclone Akvan 
 IMD steps up rain alert for Telangana under Cyclone Akvan
 The IMD, Hyderabad, has escalated rainfall warnings for several Telangana districts under Cyclone Akvan, forecasting heavy to very heavy rain, thunderstorms, lightning and squally winds from November 20. Hyderabad and surrounding districts are expected to remain largely dry.
 By 
 Telangana Today 
 Updated On - 17 November 2026, 12:20 AM 
 Hyderabad: The India Meteorological Department (IMD), Hyderabad, on Monday evening significantly scaled up its weather warnings for certain districts of Telangana under the influence of the approaching Cyclone Akvan.
 The updated weather bulletin indicates a wider spread of rainfall, affecting most parts of Telangana, even as Hyderabad and surrounding districts are expected to remain largely dry. Alerts for severe winds and heavy to very heavy rainfall have been issued for multiple districts from November 20.
 While dry and chilly weather is likely to prevail across Telangana for the next three days, weather conditions are expected to change drastically from Thursday, November 19.
 For November 19 and 20, the IMD, Hyderabad, forecast light to moderate rain or thundershowers, along with thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds (30 to 40 kmph), at isolated locations in eastern and southeastern districts, including Mulugu, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Nalgonda, Suryapet and Mahabubabad.
 Between November 20 and 21, a warning of heavy (64.5 mm to 115.5 mm) to very heavy rainfall (up to 204.4 mm), accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and squally winds (50 to 60 kmph), has been issued for isolated places in Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Suryapet and Mahabubabad districts. Heavy rainfall and squally winds of 40–50 kmph have also been forecast for Mulugu, Nalgonda, Jangaon, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri, Warangal and Hanamkonda districts.
 In its forecast for November 21 and 22, the IMD, Hyderabad, indicated heavy to very heavy rainfall, along with squally winds, at isolated places in Jayashankar Bhupalpally, Mulugu, Bhadradri Kothagudem and Khammam districts.
 Some other isolated areas in Mancherial, Karimnagar, Peddapalli, Mahabubabad, Warangal and Hanamkonda districts are also expected to witness heavy rainfall with squally winds during the same period.
